review_scope: Complete52-line enterprise configuration article and two complete single-line reusable dependencies read; all26 candidates and non-candidate headings, context and metadata accounted. Previously reviewed enterprise navigation/MCP scope fragments re-read without duplicate receipts. Twenty authored claims preserve settings routes, permissions, default-public-code and feedback boundaries. No native operation, adoption, rights or independent omission/rendering certification.

claims.statement: Enterprise owners are the declared administrators for this procedure; role metadata does not verify the current actor's actual permissions.
Enterprise configuration scope declares Business/Enterprise plans and the Copilot cloud feature; no GHES availability follows from generic navigation includes.
An organization-assigned license is governed by feature/model policies; license possession alone does not imply every feature enabled.
First-time governance guidance is separately linked; its compliance/productivity advice is not reviewed through this reference.
Enterprise owners can choose whole-enterprise policy or delegate decisions to organization owners; the linked concept's exceptions remain applicable.
Enterprise target navigation and the AI controls tab are procedural dependencies; target selection and permissions require actual verification.
AI-agent policies are on the Agents page, distinct from Copilot administration and MCP controls.
The Copilot page contains administration, privacy, model, billing and usage policies; those dimensions must not be conflated.
Feature/client policies use Configure features & clients under Copilot; other client-specific controls remain independent.
MCP policies have a separate MCP page; UI grouping does not grant third-party-host MCP access governance.
Dropdown policies require choosing an enforcement option; the documented choice is not an observed setting.
Toggle policies control availability or enforcement; actual behavior and authorization to change them remain separate.
A policy without a visible dropdown/toggle may have configuration under its name; missing immediate controls must not be treated as absent policy or PASS.
The existing MCP note limits Copilot policy to generally available support and excludes third-party-host GitHub MCP permissions; no duplicate receipt is created.
The included public-code policy fragment declares a Business Allowed default and separate Privacy setting, not rights clearance.
Feedback collection opt-in depends on enabling Copilot in GitHub.com through Features & clients; feedback is distinct from training authorization.
Per-policy conflict and supported-surface references are separately reviewed evidence; neither gives a live effective-policy receipt.
The reusable directs navigation to the AI controls tab; the icon/tab label is not actual authorization or enforcement.
The pin describes Suggestions matching public code as Allowed by default for Business users; no actual enterprise setting or copyright/license clearance is established.
The public-code default can be changed in the Copilot policy page's Privacy section; a documented route is not an applied or propagated setting.
